verdict.rationale: Conductor documents its own API for creating cloud workspaces, sending prompts to the coding agent and reading its replies. That gives scripts a non-interactive way to drive the agent. Routines also let agents run on a schedule or via a GitHub action, but this is limited to cloud workspaces and is not a local headless/CLI mode. Missing for 10: a documented non-interactive CLI/headless invocation for local scripts, API depth (no OpenAPI spec found, auth/exit-status/output-format details), and independent hands-on corroboration of scripted automation.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the agent non-interactively in scripts for workflow automation

citations.quote: Use it to do things like: Create workspaces, send prompts to the coding agent, and read its replies.
You can now run your agents on a schedule or via GitHub action.
The Conductor API lets you manage cloud workspaces programmatically.
